title: Japan sets up a team within its National Cybersecurity Office to contact companies at risk of cyberattacks, Nikkei reports
date_note: Nikkei's article, published 27 November, says the team was set up on 27 November.
geo_basis: Japanese government agency named by the source; pin at Tokyo
summary: Nikkei reports that the Japanese government set up an outreach team within the National Cybersecurity Office on 27 November, with dozens of staff. According to Nikkei, it will contact companies that may be targeted, advise them on measures, use threat hunting to look for undetected intrusions and proactively approach critical-infrastructure-linked companies. Nikkei says the team was part of an emergency package approved at a ministerial meeting on the 6th (the article gives no month).
plain: Nikkei reports Japan's government has created a team to contact companies that may be targeted by cyberattacks and advise them on defences.
exec: Companies, especially those linked to critical infrastructure, may be contacted by the new government team, according to Nikkei.
impact: Policy item; details come only from Nikkei's report.

validation.note: One publisher read (Nikkei); the government's own announcement was not read.

review.note: date: summary said package approved 6 November; Nikkei gives only 'the 6th', no month; reworded. Rest matches Nikkei
